record.narrative: No prior evidence is available, so this first iteration registers a broad, falsifiable screen for measured predictor subgroups that are associated with stronger dependency (more negative CRISPR dependency scores). I prioritized comparisons with large, complete cell sizes: mostly binary features with exposed counts well above 20, plus one categorical feature with known sufficiently large levels. Outcomes were spread across all 16 dependency scores, with early positions emphasizing higher-variance scores that are more likely to reveal large differences. Each proposal compares the predictor-positive group, or the non-modal level_002 for feature_054, against the predictor-negative/modal level, expecting a negative exposed-minus-comparator mean difference, i.e., stronger dependency in the exposed group. Direction is set to -1 to make the evidence signed to that same stronger-dependency hypothesis. These are association hypotheses in this dataset only, not causal claims. Later I will judge whether point estimates and 95% intervals imply differences large enough relative to the 10% clinical-significance guideline, and then pursue interactions or validation only for promising main-effect signals.

This is the first analysis wave, so I selected 12 registered main-effect comparisons that combine adequate cell sizes with outcomes likely to make a 10% relative dependency-score difference detectable and meaningful. H1-H6 prioritize higher-dispersion dependency scores and relatively prevalent binary exposures or larger categorical contrasts, giving good power to estimate group mean differences and supporting follow-up if effect sizes are clinically relevant. H7-H12 extend the screen to additional outcomes and predictors, including one non-modal categorical level contrast, while still satisfying the 20-observation cell-size constraint. The remaining registered comparisons (H13-H16) are deferred for this wave because they involve lower exposure prevalence or less promising initial signal-prioritization; I will carry them forward if the first-wave evidence suggests broader association patterns or if sample-size-adjusted estimates are needed.

All twelve first-wave main-effect tests are null for the pre-specified stronger-dependency hypothesis. The signed estimates are small and every 95% interval includes zero, so none of H1-H12 can be accepted. I judged clinical importance relative to the observed outcome scale: 10% of the absolute mean dependency score for each outcome is roughly 0.009 to 0.042. For H1, H5, H8, H10, and H11, the positive upper bounds are below that scale-based clinical threshold, so I reject the scientifically meaningful version of those claims in this dataset and close those lines. For the remaining unresolved lines, especially H2, H3, H4, H6, H9, and H12, the intervals still include clinically meaningful positive differences despite small point estimates, so the data cannot rule them out; these remain active for refinement or continued screening. H7 is borderline (upper bound only slightly above the scale-based threshold) and is deferred rather than actively prioritized. I am not requesting validation because no claim is accepted and none shows a clear clinically meaningful signal; validation would be better spent on a later claim with clearer evidence.

No validation was requested or delivered, and there are no response deadlines to reassess. The current evidence therefore remains an interim negative/broad-screen result rather than a set of supported claims. In this dataset, none of the twelve first-wave stronger-dependency associations is accepted: all 95% intervals include zero, and several positive upper bounds are below a conservative scale-aware 10% clinical benchmark (approximate 10% of the absolute mean dependency score). Claims H1, H5, H8, H10, and H11 are rejected/closed; H2, H3, H4, H6, H9, and H12 remain unresolved because their intervals do not exclude clinically meaningful positive differences, though their point estimates are modest; H7 is deferred. No causal or generalizable conclusions can be drawn: these are associations among opaque measured predictors and dependency-score outcomes, with multiplicity and biological interpretation unresolved. I propose a second round of main-effect comparisons focused on high-power binary predictors and high-variance dependency scores, especially outcome_001, outcome_014, outcome_006, outcome_013, outcome_008, and outcome_011. These new proposals use prevalent complete binary features with cell sizes well above the minimum, maximizing the ability to detect effects near the clinical threshold. Interactions are not yet justified because no first-wave main effect has shown a clinically meaningful signal. Validation is still premature; the next analysis wave should complete the registered screen (including H13-H16) and add these higher-powered comparisons before validating any claim.

There are no new assessment deadlines, so I am not reassessing claims in this exploration step. The first-wave evidence is broadly negative or only marginally suggestive: several main effects are rejected because their positive upper bounds do not reach a conservative scale-aware 10% clinical benchmark, while the remaining unresolved lines have modest point estimates and intervals that cannot support acceptance. I therefore propose a second, better-powered screen plus a small set of interaction refinements. The new main-effect proposals add predictors that were not previously tested and that have complete binary cells large enough for Welch tests: feature_064, feature_005, feature_007, feature_022, feature_029, feature_062, feature_032, feature_001, and feature_046. I also test feature_054 on high-variance outcomes because its level_002-level_001 contrast was the most suggestive first-wave result and both cells are large and known. I extend the broad screen to outcome_004, outcome_009, outcome_010, and outcome_003 with complete prevalent predictors, even though these outcomes have lower variance, to avoid limiting the search to only the highest-variance dependencies. Finally, because main effects may be masked or heterogeneous, I propose three interaction refinements with large marginal cells: outcome_006/feature_034 modified by feature_030, outcome_013/feature_045 modified by feature_030, and outcome_014/feature_060 modified by feature_042. All hypotheses remain dataset-specific association tests, not causal or generalizable claims; acceptance will require an interval that clearly supports a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency effect.

No assessment deadlines are due, so no claim status changes are made at this analyze stage. I request twelve discovery analyses that combine completion of the previously registered broad screen with higher-powered second-wave associations. H13-H16 complete the first-wave register and add outcomes 004, 009, 010, and 003 using predictors with adequate exposed-cell sizes. H17-H24 begin the higher-powered second wave, prioritizing complete binary predictors with large cells (features 008, 030, 042, and 023) and outcomes where the first wave either remained unresolved or had enough dispersion to make clinically meaningful differences detectable (outcomes 001, 014, 006, and 013). I defer additional low-prevalence predictors, feature 054 repeat tests, and interaction refinements until there is evidence that one of these main-effect comparisons supports a clinically meaningful signal.

I assessed the twelve new discovery results against the task's 10% clinical benchmark using a conservative scale-aware threshold: 0.10 times the absolute mean of the relevant dependency score. Approximate thresholds were outcome_001 0.0415, outcome_006 0.0175, outcome_013 0.0269, outcome_014 0.0093, outcome_004 0.0255, outcome_009 0.0256, outcome_010 0.0252, and outcome_003 0.0253. H16 is the only clear null rejection: its signed estimate is slightly opposite the hypothesized direction and its 95% upper bound is below the clinical threshold, so I reject and close it. For several other comparisons, the point estimate is small or negative but the 95% upper bound still reaches or exceeds the clinical threshold; these cannot be rejected as ruling out a meaningful stronger-dependency effect, but they also provide no basis to accept. H13, H14, H15, H17, H18, H20, H22, and H24 are therefore left unresolved and deferred rather than actively prioritized, mostly because the evidence is either imprecise, low prevalence, or inconsistent with a coherent pattern. The strongest discovery signals all involve feature_042: H19 in outcome_001 has estimate 0.04395 with a positive 95% interval [0.00346, 0.08444]; H21 in outcome_014 has estimate 0.03511 and is nearly significant [-0.00119, 0.07141]; and H23 in outcome_006 has the largest relative effect, estimate 0.05342 with a positive interval [0.01145, 0.09539]. However, none of these intervals has a lower bound above the 10%-relative clinical threshold, and many comparisons have been screened, so I am not accepting any at discovery. I request independent validation for H23 because it is the most clinically compelling candidate: the point estimate is about 30% of the absolute outcome_006 mean, its interval excludes zero, and the direction is consistent with the pre-specified stronger-dependency hypothesis. I also registered follow-up feature_042 main-effect tests on additional dependency scores and one feature_042 interaction refinement linked to H23, so that the next analysis can test whether this predictor shows a broader or subgroup-dependent association. These remain dataset-specific association findings, not causal or generalizable claims.

The only due reassessment is H23. Its discovery result R23 was the strongest feature_042 main-effect signal: for outcome_006, the signed estimate was +0.0534 with a 95% interval [0.0114, 0.0954]. The point estimate exceeds the scale-aware 10% clinical threshold for outcome_006 (about 0.0175) and the interval excludes zero, but the lower confidence limit does not exceed the clinical threshold. The independent validation R25 is much less favorable: the signed estimate is -0.0091 with an adjusted interval [-0.0653, 0.0471]. This validation result is in the opposite direction, includes zero, and provides no independent evidence of a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency association. It does not strictly rule out a positive effect because the upper bound remains positive, but given the discovery threshold ambiguity, multiple comparisons, and failed replication, the exact outcome_006/feature_042 main-effect claim is not supported as an accepted dataset-specific association. I therefore reject and close H23. I also downgrade H19 and H21 from active to deferred: they remain unresolved positive discovery signals for feature_042 on outcome_001 and outcome_014, but their intervals do not establish clinically meaningful stronger dependency, and the strongest feature_042 validation failed. No claims are currently accepted. The next analysis wave should prioritize the registered feature_042 follow-up tests H47-H50 to determine whether any coherent broader or subgroup-specific pattern remains, and then high-power untested predictors. Validation should be reserved for a future claim with clearer discovery evidence or replication support.

No assessment deadlines are due, so no claim statuses are changed in this exploration step. The current evidence has not yet produced an accepted association. The strongest discovery signal was feature_042 on outcome_006, but independent validation was discordant and null, so H23 was rejected and closed. I will still let the registered feature_042 follow-ups H47-H50 run, because they can tell us whether the signal is restricted to one outcome or appears conditionally, but I will not prioritize feature_042 further until those results are available. Meanwhile, I propose high-power main-effect refinements around the remaining unresolved balanced binary predictors feature_034, feature_060, and feature_002. These predictors have roughly balanced groups near 1,000 observations per cell, giving substantially more precision than many previously tested low-prevalence binary predictors. I extend feature_034 to outcome_014, outcome_008, outcome_011, and outcome_013; feature_060 to outcome_006, outcome_013, outcome_008, and outcome_011; and feature_002 to outcome_006 and outcome_014. These outcomes are selected because they have relatively high dispersion or comparatively low absolute 10%-relative clinical thresholds: approximately outcome_014 0.0093, outcome_006 0.0175, outcome_013 0.0269, outcome_008 0.0282, and outcome_011 0.0301. The hypotheses are dataset-specific association tests: exposed=1 versus comparator=0 for the named predictor, with direction -1 meaning we are testing whether the exposed group has more negative dependency scores. I set anticipated_direction=0 because predictor labels are opaque and prior evidence is too weak to justify a strong directional expectation beyond the stated stronger-dependency claim. Acceptance will require evidence that the clinically meaningful stronger-dependency effect is supported in this dataset; causal or generalizable interpretation remains outside scope.

No assessment deadlines are due, so no claim status changes are made at this analyze stage. I request twelve untested discovery comparisons. First, H47-H50 complete the registered feature_042 follow-up wave: main effects on outcome_013, outcome_011, and outcome_008, plus an outcome_006 interaction with feature_030. These are justified because feature_042 produced the strongest discovery signals so far (outcome_001, outcome_014, and especially outcome_006), while the strongest outcome_006 main effect failed independent validation. The follow-ups will tell us whether feature_042 is associated with stronger dependency across other outcomes, or whether any remaining signal is restricted to a subgroup. Second, I request H51-H54 and H55-H58, extending the balanced binary predictors feature_034 and feature_060 to outcomes with relatively high variance or low absolute 10%-relative clinical thresholds. Both predictors have nearly balanced cells near 1,000 observations per group, giving better precision than many previously tested low-prevalence predictors. Their prior unresolved results were modest, but broader outcome coverage is needed before closing these predictor lines. I defer feature_002 follow-ups H59-H60 and other registered broad-screen claims until these focused predictor patterns are visible. These requests are dataset-specific association tests; any accepted conclusion will require uncertainty intervals that support a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency difference, not causal or generalizable interpretation.

No claim is accepted at this appraise stage. I judged the 12 new results against scale-aware 10% clinical benchmarks: approximately outcome_013 0.0269, outcome_008 0.0282, outcome_011 0.0301, outcome_006 0.0175, and outcome_014 0.0093. H47, H54, and H58 are directional claims whose signed intervals either lie mostly opposite or have upper confidence bounds far below the corresponding clinical threshold, so they do not support clinically meaningful stronger dependency and are closed. H49 is especially informative against the original stronger-dependency hypothesis: the signed estimate is negative with a 95% interval entirely below zero, indicating the opposite direction, so H49 is rejected and closed. I am not currently proposing a reversed claim because the reversed lower bound would still not clearly exceed the clinical threshold and the feature_042 pattern is discordant overall. The feature_042 follow-ups also failed to produce a coherent pattern: outcome_013 and outcome_011 are near null, the outcome_006/feature_030 interaction is extremely imprecise, and the strongest earlier outcome_006 main effect already failed independent validation. The feature_034 follow-ups are mostly small or null; H54 rules out the stronger-dependency direction for outcome_013, while other outcomes remain too weak or imprecise to pursue. The feature_060 follow-ups are similar, except H55 is the closest candidate: outcome_006 has a point estimate above the 0.0175 threshold, but its interval includes zero and therefore does not support acceptance or validation yet. I therefore request no independent validation in this round and will prioritize remaining high-power untested main effects, especially feature_002 and feature_047 extensions, before spending validation on any borderline signal.

No new validation result or assessment deadline was delivered in this synthesis stage, so I changed no claim statuses on evidence grounds. The supported finding set remains empty under the stated clinical criterion. Using a conservative scale-aware interpretation of a 10% or greater clinically meaningful difference in dependency score, no comparison currently has a lower confidence bound above the relevant threshold, and the strongest prior feature_042 signal failed independent validation and does not have a coherent multi-outcome follow-up pattern. The closed negative findings are informative: several predictors show intervals incompatible with clinically meaningful stronger dependency, and the outcome_008/feature_042 comparison is robustly in the opposite direction. I do not accept a reversed feature_042/outcome_008 claim because the reversed lower confidence bound remains below the clinical threshold and the broader feature_042 pattern is inconsistent. The main unresolved uncertainty is in borderline or low-power main effects, especially H55, whose point estimate exceeds the outcome_006 threshold but whose interval includes zero and therefore does not justify acceptance or validation. The next analysis wave should prioritize the registered high-precision feature_002 and feature_047 comparisons H59-H65. If those are null, close these predictor lines and move toward broader categorical or continuous predictor screening, reserving validation for effects whose uncertainty intervals support clinically meaningful differences rather than merely large point estimates. Any accepted conclusion would still be dataset-specific association evidence, not causal or generalizable.

No assessment deadlines are due, so I make no status changes at this exploration stage. The existing untested high-precision comparisons H59-H65 remain the first analysis priority: they extend the balanced binary predictor feature_002 and the moderately prevalent binary predictor feature_047 to outcomes with favorable scale and precision, especially outcome_014 and outcome_006. To avoid wasting later analysis capacity on lower-power rare-predictor screens, I additionally register high-power extensions of feature_045 and feature_054. feature_045 has 510 versus 1490 cells and a prior positive signed signal on outcome_013 (H4/R4), while feature_054 has 578 versus 1422 cells and a prior positive signed signal on outcome_007 (H12/R12). I test each across low clinical-threshold or high-dispersion outcomes: outcome_014 (threshold about 0.0093), outcome_006 (0.0175), outcome_013 (0.0269), outcome_008 (0.0282), outcome_011 (0.0301), and outcome_001 (0.0415), using scale-aware 10% absolute-mean benchmarks. Direction -1 tests whether the exposed group has a more negative dependency score; anticipated_direction -1 reflects the raw negative prior pattern that would correspond to a positive signed result. These are dataset-specific association hypotheses only. Acceptance will require uncertainty intervals that support a clinically meaningful difference, not merely an elevated point estimate; causal or generalizable interpretation remains outside scope.

No assessment deadlines are due, so I make no status changes at this analyze stage. I select twelve untested discovery comparisons that complete the two most important high-precision binary predictor lines and add two focused feature_045 follow-ups. First, I complete feature_002 on outcome_006, outcome_014, outcome_013, outcome_008, and outcome_011 (H59-H63). feature_002 is nearly balanced (~989 vs ~1011 in the earlier outcome_001 test), so these tests have good precision for outcomes with scale-aware 10% clinical thresholds roughly 0.0175 (outcome_006), 0.0093 (outcome_014), 0.0269 (outcome_013), 0.0282 (outcome_008), and 0.0301 (outcome_011). Second, I complete feature_047 on the same five outcomes (H64, H65, H25, H26, H27). feature_047 is less balanced (~1,617 vs ~383 in earlier similar feature_064 cell sizes) but still has adequate cell counts and has not been tested on these outcomes. Third, I test feature_045 on outcome_014 and outcome_006 (H66-H67), the two untested feature_045 extensions with the lowest clinical thresholds and highest potential for a scientifically meaningful result if the prior outcome_013 signal is directionally replicated. I defer the new feature_054 extensions because its prior signed signal (outcome_007 point estimate 0.0145) is below the corresponding clinical threshold (~0.0245) and is less compelling than the feature_045 low-threshold follow-ups. These analyses are dataset-specific association tests; direction -1 tests whether the exposed group has more negative dependency scores. Acceptance will require 95% discovery intervals that support a clinically meaningful difference, not merely point estimates above threshold.

I assessed the 12 new discovery results against scale-aware 10% clinical thresholds. No result has a 95% confidence interval that confidently reaches the clinically meaningful range, so no claim is accepted. Three comparisons rule out clinically meaningful stronger dependency in the claimed direction and are rejected/closed: H61/R40 has upper bound 0.0235 below outcome_013 threshold about 0.0269; H63/R42 has upper bound 0.0105 below outcome_011 threshold about 0.0301; and H25/R45 is opposite in direction with upper bound 0.0016 below outcome_013 threshold. The only promising discovery is H26/R46: feature_047 on outcome_008 gives signed difference +0.02822, with a 95% interval [0.00187, 0.05457]. It excludes zero in the stronger-dependency direction and is essentially at the 10% absolute-mean threshold (rounded threshold about 0.0282), but the lower bound is far below threshold, so clinically meaningful magnitude is uncertain. feature_047 is also discordant across outcomes: H25 is opposite/negative, H64-H65 are imprecise, and H27 is null. Given multiplicity and the prior failed validation of a strong feature_042 signal, I do not accept H26 on discovery evidence alone. I request independent validation for H26 as the single most plausible candidate. The remaining unresolved results are kept deferred because their intervals either do not rule out clinically meaningful effects but provide no compelling support, or point in uninformative directions: H59/R38, H60/R39, H62/R41, H64/R43, H65/R44, H27/R47, H66/R48, and H67/R49. Overall, feature_002 and feature_045 do not show coherent clinically meaningful stronger-dependency patterns.

Both validation results delivered for this synthesis stage fail to support the original stronger-dependency claims. For H23, outcome_006 feature_042 had a discovery signed mean difference of +0.0534, but the 95% discovery interval [0.0114, 0.0954] did not rule in the scale-aware 10% benchmark for outcome_006 (~0.0175). Independent validation R25 gives a signed difference of -0.0091 with independent interval [-0.0653, 0.0471], i.e., the validation estimate is opposite to the discovery claim. Although the independent interval does not exclude all clinically meaningful positive effects, the combined discovery-plus-validation pattern provides no supported clinically meaningful association, and feature_042 is already inconsistent across outcomes (notably outcome_008 opposite). I therefore keep H23 rejected and closed. For H26, outcome_008 feature_047 was the strongest remaining discovery candidate: signed difference +0.0282, interval [0.0019, 0.0546], point estimate essentially at the outcome_008 clinical benchmark (~0.0282). Independent validation R50 gives signed difference -0.0039 with independent interval [-0.0477, 0.0400], a failure to replicate and an opposite point estimate. This is reinforced by the discordant feature_047 pattern: outcome_013 is opposite and rejected (H25), outcome_011 is null (H27), and outcome_006/outcome_014 are imprecise (H64/H65). I therefore reject H26 as a supported association and close the investigation. Overall, under the conservative scale-aware interpretation that clinically meaningful evidence requires uncertainty intervals that rule in a 10%-or-greater effect or a coherent replicated pattern, no claim is accepted. The supported finding set remains empty in this dataset. Informative negative findings include multiple intervals incompatible with clinically meaningful stronger dependency and several opposite-direction findings. Remaining uncertainty is mainly in borderline, nonreplicated, or low-precision comparisons. Next, I should allocate analysis to the strongest untested high-power registered follow-ups, especially feature_054 level_002 versus level_001 across outcomes with favorable thresholds and cells, then feature_045 outcome_008/011 extensions, before spending further validation capacity. Validation should be reserved for discovery intervals that already rule in clinically meaningful effects or for emerging multi-outcome replication, not for isolated borderline point estimates.

No assessment deadlines are due, so this exploration stage registers new comparisons and one reversal/refinement. The main untested priority remains feature_054 level_002 versus level_001 because it has adequate cell sizes (~578 versus ~1422) and a prior borderline stronger-dependency signal on outcome_007 (R12: signed +0.0145, below the outcome_007 threshold about 0.0245). I propose a complete feature_054 panel across the remaining outcomes, prioritizing outcomes with low scale-aware clinical thresholds and favorable variance: outcome_015, outcome_002, outcome_003, outcome_004, outcome_005, outcome_009, outcome_010, outcome_012, and outcome_016. These are dataset-specific association hypotheses for stronger dependency in level_002 versus level_001. Second, feature_008 is highly prevalent and has borderline prior signals on outcome_006 and outcome_014; I extend it to outcome_008, outcome_011, outcome_013, and outcome_007, which have thresholds roughly 0.0282, 0.0301, 0.0269, and 0.0245, respectively. Third, the reversed claim for feature_042 on outcome_008 is scientifically useful because the earlier stronger-dependency claim H49 was opposite: the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast was positive about 0.0295, just above the outcome_008 clinical benchmark, with an interval excluding zero in that opposite direction. A new direction +1 claim asks whether this represents a clinically meaningful weaker-dependency association, though uncertainty still leaves clinical magnitude uncertain. Fourth, I register balanced interaction/subgroup comparisons using fully observed binary predictors with expected adequate four-cell counts. These avoid the sparse-subgroup problem that caused very wide intervals in prior feature_030-based interactions and test whether associations for feature_002, feature_034, or feature_054 differ by another measured predictor. Finally, I add feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 on outcome_014 and outcome_006 as a limited broadening to an untested categorical predictor with a plausible level distribution. Analysis capacity should first take the strongest feature_054 and feature_008 follow-ups plus the reversed feature_042/outcome_008 candidate, then balanced interactions if main-effect capacity remains. Acceptance will require uncertainty that rules in clinically meaningful differences or coherent replicated patterns; all conclusions remain associations in this dataset, not causal or generalizable claims.

No assessment deadlines are due, so this stage requests analyses only. I select twelve untested discovery comparisons that follow the strongest high-power prior signal while adding one alternative predictor line to avoid overconcentration. The feature_054 level_002-versus-level_001 comparison has adequate cells and a prior borderline positive signed signal on outcome_007 (R12), so I test it across outcomes where scale-aware 10% absolute-mean benchmarks are low or favorable and where uncertainty can potentially rule in or rule out a clinically meaningful difference. H34 and H32 address the low clinical benchmarks for outcome_014 and outcome_006; H74, H75, H76, H77, H78, H79, H80, H81, and H82 complete the feature_054 panel over outcome_015, outcome_002, outcome_003, outcome_004, outcome_005, outcome_009, outcome_010, outcome_012, and outcome_016. I also include H86, feature_008 on outcome_007, because feature_008 is highly prevalent and already shows imprecise but positive low-threshold points on outcome_014 and outcome_006, providing one alternative predictor follow-up. I do not request H87 because it reuses existing evidence R28 and would not provide a new sample; it can be assessed or validated later if warranted. All directions are -1, so a positive signed estimate indicates the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. Acceptance will require intervals that rule in clinically meaningful differences or coherent replicated patterns, not merely point estimates above threshold; these remain dataset-specific association tests.

I assessed the 12 newly delivered discovery results using the same scale-aware 10% absolute-mean clinical benchmarks. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate indicates stronger dependency in the exposed group. No new result has a 95% lower bound above the corresponding clinical threshold, so none is accepted. Nine results have upper confidence bounds below the scale-aware threshold and therefore rule out clinically meaningful stronger dependency in the claimed direction: H74/R53, H75/R54, H76/R55, H77/R56, H78/R57, H79/R58, H80/R59, H81/R60, and H82/R61. Most of these point estimates are near zero or opposite to the claimed stronger-dependency direction, reinforcing that feature_054 level_002 versus level_001 is not showing a coherent clinically meaningful stronger-dependency pattern across outcomes. H34/R51 and H32/R52 remain unresolved because their upper bounds extend above the low thresholds for outcome_014 and outcome_006, but their point estimates are negative or near zero and the intervals do not provide support for accepting the claim. H86/R62 for feature_008 on outcome_007 remains unresolved because its interval includes both clinically meaningful positive effects and nonmeaningful/opposite effects; the point estimate is below threshold and the prior feature_008 pattern is not coherent. I request no independent validation because none of these results has a discovery lower bound above the clinical threshold, and the feature_054 and feature_008 patterns are not replicated sufficiently to justify spending validation capacity.

No validation response deadlines are open for this synthesis stage, and no new validation evidence has arrived. The current supported claim set remains empty. Under the scale-aware 10% absolute-mean benchmark, the strongest discovery candidates have not produced intervals whose lower bound rules in a clinically meaningful 10%-or-greater association, and the two prior independent validations failed to replicate the original directions. For H23, feature_042 on outcome_006 had a promising discovery estimate but independent validation reversed the point estimate. For H26, feature_047 on outcome_008 had a discovery estimate near the outcome-specific threshold, but independent validation also failed to replicate and pointed opposite. Therefore, the scientifically supported conclusion in this dataset is still absence of a confirmed clinically meaningful association. Informative negative findings include the feature_054 level_002-versus-level_001 panel across outcome_015, outcome_002, outcome_003, outcome_004, outcome_005, outcome_009, outcome_010, outcome_012, and outcome_016, where intervals rule out clinically meaningful stronger dependency, and multiple binary contrasts for feature_002, feature_045, feature_034, feature_060, feature_047, and feature_042 that are near-null, opposite, or nonreplicated. Remaining uncertainty is concentrated in low-threshold but interval-limited signals, especially feature_042 on outcome_014 and reversed feature_042 on outcome_008, plus feature_060 and feature_045 main effects on low-threshold outcomes. The most informative next analyses are registered here as follow-ups: complete high-value untested feature_045 lines, test feature_063 and feature_055 categorical contrasts on outcome_014 and outcome_006, and use balanced binary interactions to examine whether feature_042 or feature_060 associations differ by other fully observed predictors. Validation should remain reserved for claims that either achieve interval-level clinical magnitude or show a newly coherent multi-outcome pattern; in particular, H21 and H87 are the best future validation candidates if the pattern remains stable.

No assessment deadlines are due, so this stage registers refinements that ask whether the strongest remaining borderline candidates are concentrated in clinically meaningful subgroups. The feature_042 line is the best current candidate: H21 on outcome_014 is a stronger-dependency claim with signed estimate 0.0351 and 95% interval about [-0.0012, 0.0714], while H87 on outcome_008 is a reversed weaker-dependency claim with signed estimate 0.0295 and interval about [0.0055, 0.0536]. Their overall intervals still do not rule in the scale-aware 10% benchmark. I therefore test the same contrasts within balanced fully observed binary subgroups defined by feature_002, feature_034, or feature_060. If the association is concentrated in one subgroup, the subgroup lower bound could reach clinical magnitude, whereas if estimates are similar to the parent main effects or intervals remain wide, the candidate remains unsupported or can be closed. For feature_042, direction -1 on outcome_014 asks whether feature_042=1 versus 0 has a more negative score, i.e. stronger dependency, inside each subgroup. Direction +1 on outcome_008 asks whether feature_042=1 versus 0 has a less negative score, i.e. weaker dependency, inside each subgroup. I add analogous refinements for H104, the reversed feature_045 outcome_014 weaker-dependency candidate, because its signed estimate 0.0218 is above the low outcome_014 benchmark but its interval includes clinically null and opposite effects. Plausible alternatives include: subgroup estimates remain nonclinical, subgroup differences arise from correlations among binary predictors, or reversed associations are artifacts of outcome-specific scaling or selection. These are dataset-specific association hypotheses; they are not causal claims. The subgroup definitions are intentionally balanced to preserve cell counts and avoid the wide intervals seen in earlier sparse feature_030 interactions.

No assessment deadlines are due, so this stage requests twelve new discovery analyses. First, I request the nine directly interpretable subgroup refinements H105-H113. These are the most informative immediate follow-ups to the strongest unresolved candidates: feature_042 on outcome_014 and reversed feature_042 on outcome_008, and feature_045 on outcome_014. H105-H107 test feature_042=1 versus 0 within feature_002=1, feature_034=1, or feature_060=1 for outcome_014 with direction -1; a positive signed estimate means more negative dependency, i.e. stronger dependency. H108-H110 test the same feature_042 contrast for outcome_008 with direction +1; a positive signed estimate means less negative dependency, i.e. weaker dependency. H111-H113 test feature_045=1 versus 0 for outcome_014 with direction +1, again asking whether feature_045 exposure is associated with less negative dependency within balanced binary strata. These subgroup mean_difference analyses can either concentrate clinical magnitude into a specific stratum or provide informative nulls if the subgroup estimates remain nonclinical. The second part of the analysis request adds three low-threshold broadening contrasts to avoid placing all remaining capacity on the correlated feature_042/feature_045 line. H92 and H93 test feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 on outcome_014 and outcome_006, two outcomes with relatively low scale-aware clinical benchmarks. H98 tests feature_055 level_002 versus level_003 on outcome_014. These direction -1 claims ask whether the exposed category has stronger dependency; positive estimates indicate stronger dependency. If their upper confidence bounds fall below the relevant 10% absolute-mean benchmark, we can close those new categorical lines; if a lower bound rules in clinical magnitude, they become future validation candidates. I do not request H87 or other already tested claims because they would reuse existing evidence and not add new samples. All conclusions from these analyses remain dataset-specific associations unless independently validated.

I assessed the twelve new discovery results using the same scale-aware clinical benchmark: a 95% signed lower bound must exceed roughly 10% of the absolute outcome mean to accept a clinically meaningful association in the claimed direction.
